title: Hybrid 2D Sprite + 3D Campaign Visual Architecture
nonNegotiables: Player Deities, player characters, enemy characters, enemy deities, units, and combatants are 2D sprites.
Campaign maps, Realms, exploration spaces, gates, major locations, and tactical environments are 3D environments.
Do not convert battlefield characters into 3D models because the environment is 3D.
Do not introduce futuristic craft or sci-fi spacecraft; Realm travel remains Gate-based.
Preview and Visual QA must show sprites and environments together before approval.

visualLayers.name: 2D Sprites
visualLayers.purpose: Character identity, tactical readability, faction recognition, combat clarity

visualLayers.name: 3D Environments
visualLayers.purpose: World scale, atmospheric depth, exploration, campaign progression, Realm identity

visualLayers.name: 2D Portraits
visualLayers.purpose: Profile identity, Codex presentation, emotional read, dialogue scenes

visualLayers.name: Cinematic Art
visualLayers.purpose: Major story beats, chapter reveals, faction presentation moments

requirements: The path physically exists in the 3D Realm environment.
Distance, direction, terrain, landmarks, Gates, battles, boss encounters, and progression must be visible.
Campaign sections load in manageable regions rather than loading the entire world.
Gate landmarks act as transitions, objectives, and Realm travel anchors.
mobileCameraRules: No complicated open-world camera unless gameplay requires it

requirements: Sprites must align with tile/grid positioning and perspective.
Selection circles and movement indicators must ground sprites in the 3D space.
Terrain should not hide key sprites at mobile camera angles.
Titan scale may be larger than normal characters, but must remain consistent and intentional.

blockedContexts: Tile/grid combatant if no sprite exists unless temporary placeholder is clearly marked

assetTypes.definition: Dimensional travel landmark and objective object
blockedContexts: Futuristic craft replacement or sci-fi vehicle

performanceRules: Use optimized meshes and texture compression.
Divide elongated campaign maps into manageable regions.
Stream or load only the current campaign section where possible.
Use level-of-detail systems for large Realm environments.
Use efficient lighting and limited unnecessary geometry.
Flag oversized 3D assets and oversized sprites before approval.
